goal: Harmonize a raw 15-country climate-attitudes survey with Meta/Yale 2023 and ESS Round 8 (Poortinga et al. 2018) benchmarks. Deliver harmonized_survey.db (cleaned_responses with quality flags, variable_crosswalk, country_metadata), a 5-sheet cross_study_analysis.xlsx (Country_Benchmarks with differences and N/A for non-overlap, descriptives, correlations, two OLS models, Divergence_Flags with explanations), and a reconciliation memo with specific recommendations for qualifying comparisons.
delivered: harmonized_survey.db: 4 misspellings and 3 blanks handled, codebook-exact crosswalk, 15-country metadata. cross_study_analysis.xlsx: a wide Country_Benchmarks with belief and worry vs Meta/Yale and ESS 'changing' only, plus Descriptive_Stats, Correlation_Matrix, Regression_Models and 29 Divergence_Flags rows. reconciliation_memo.docx covers mapping imperfections, the three-country alignment and recommendations.
what_went_wrong: The agent fetched the full ESS PDF (step 8, 20 pages) but took only Table 1's 'climate changing' column. It omitted the human-caused and bad-impacts ESS values for France/Germany/UK even though the local survey has cc_cause. It also left non-overlapping countries' ESS cells blank despite the explicit 'marked N/A' instruction (R0). All 29 Divergence_Flags rows share one boilerplate sentence, even citing '(for ESS) fieldwork timing' on Meta/Yale rows (R1). The memo labels fieldwork years but never recommends treating 2016-17 ESS as historical context rather than a direct benchmark (R5).

failed_items.why: Country_Benchmarks has ess_belief_changing_pct (96.3/95.4/93.6) but no ESS human-caused (93.8/94.8/91.0) or bad-impacts (73.7/77.4/66.0) values, though the fetched PDF contained Table 1. Non-overlap ESS cells are None, not 'N/A' as the prompt required. The wide, non-'Variable' layout also failed the rubric's schema criterion, which the prompt did not specify.

Every flag row has the same text, 'likely reflects different question wording, response threshold, sampling/frame, and (for ESS) fieldwork timing', with only the pp value changing. It gives no country-specific factor and no mention of local n of 40-72, though the agent had those counts.

The memo recommends CIs, ranks comparisons and hedges >15pp gaps (3 of 4 sub-criteria passed). For ESS it only says 'Label every external comparison with the fieldwork year' and still calls ESS a benchmark, never advising historical-context framing for the 6-7 year gap the prompt highlighted.
